correctness.rationale: The proof is an exact invariant count: \(\delta(\text{cusp})=1\), \(\delta(\text{node})=1\), and equigenericity fixes the total delta. For \(\kappa\) cusps and no other singularities, total delta is \(\kappa\), so a nodal member in the same stratum has \(\kappa\) nodes, not \(2\kappa\).

evidence: The preprint’s Theorem 4.2 says each cusp is replaced by two nodes, then says the total node count is exactly \(\delta(C)\) (PDF page 10).
For a reduced plane curve, total delta is the sum of local delta invariants; each ordinary cusp and each ordinary node contributes \(1\).
broader_coverage.reasoning: The count obstruction applies uniformly to every number \(\kappa\) of cusps: a curve with exactly \(\kappa\) cusps has total delta \(\kappa\), so a nodal curve in the same equigeneric stratum has \(\kappa\) nodes. The claimed \(2\kappa\) count is incompatible unless other delta contributions are explicitly present.
